items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1593

SPONSOR: O'MARA
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public authorities law, in relation to prohibiting
the metropolitan transportation authority from disallowing the adver-
tisement of alcohol products

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This bill would amend the Public Authorities Law by prohibiting the MTA
from banning advertisements promoting alcohol beverages on their proper-
ty.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of this bill states that the MTA shall not disallow advertise-
ments that promote any alcoholic beverages on their property.

Section 2 sets an immediate effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

New York State is currently home to our thriving beer, wine, liquor and
cider industries. The State has committed to promoting this industry
especially through tourism and the TASTE NY program. The MTA's recent
ban on advertising that promotes this strategic upstate industry is
contrary to New York State's policy and diminishes the state's overall
investments in growing this sector. In addition, revenue from alcohol
advertisements brought in almost four million dollars in gross revenue
for the MTA, an authority that is currently financially struggling. By
allowing alcohol, advertisements on the metropolitan areas mass trans-
portation vehicles and stations it would better promote our State's
beverage industry as well as bring in much needed income for the MTA.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2018 - S 7881

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately.

summary: Provides that the metropolitan transportation authority shall not disallow advertisements that promote any alcoholic beverage.
